MultipleChoice.prompt: A deploy workflow is triggered by many events, but its single job has an `if` condition so that only some runs actually deploy. The author moves `concurrency: { group: deploy, cancel-in-progress: false }` from the workflow level down to the deploy job. What problem does this move avoid?
options: The currently running deployment would be cancelled immediately, because `cancel-in-progress: false` only applies at job level.
Skipped runs would stay queued forever and block the group until someone cancels them manually.
The group would stop serializing deploy runs, so two real deployments could run at the same time.
A run that will be skipped by the job's `if` could still enter the workflow-level group and replace a pending real run, which then gets cancelled.

questions.explanation: With a workflow-level group, every triggered run enters the group even if its job is later skipped by `if`, and since only one run can be pending, a skipped run can replace a pending real run. Putting the group on the job means a job skipped by `if` never acquires the group, so it cannot displace the pending real run.

MultipleChoice.prompt: A workflow restores a compiled binary with actions/cache using a key built from hashFiles over only the main source directory, and skips the build steps when steps.<id>.outputs.cache-hit == 'true'. A developer then changes only Cargo.lock (a dependency version) and pushes. What is the most likely consequence?
options: GitHub invalidates the cache automatically whenever any file in the repository changes, so the key contents do not matter for correctness.
The cache-hit output is 'true' only if the restored binary passes a checksum comparison against a fresh build, so stale binaries are detected.
A change to a source file or the lockfile not covered by hashFiles still produces a cache hit, so the build is skipped and the old binary is reused.
The build step still runs on a hit and simply overwrites the restored binary, so an incomplete key only wastes cache storage.

questions.explanation: On a cache hit the build is skipped and the restored binary is used as-is, so the key must be derived from every input that changes the binary. If the key only hashes some files, a change to an unhashed input still hits the cache and silently ships a stale binary. Cache-hit gating does not rebuild or validate anything on its own.

MultipleChoice.prompt: A workflow grades a pull request when a bot's own comment is edited to tick a "grade" checkbox. It is triggered by `issue_comment`. Without extra filtering, people tick other checkboxes, edit their own comments, and other bots post comments, and each of these starts a run. What is the right way to prevent those unwanted runs?
options: Add a job-level `if` that checks the event action, the comment author login, and that the body contains the ticked grade box
Check the author and body inside a script step after checkout, since job-level `if` expressions cannot read the event payload
Add `types: [edited]` under the `issue_comment` trigger, since that alone limits runs to the bot's own comment
Rely on branch filters on the `issue_comment` trigger to restrict which comments start the workflow

questions.explanation: The `issue_comment` trigger fires for every comment on every issue or PR, so the workflow cannot narrow it at the event level. A job-level `if` that checks the action, the comment author login, and the body content skips runs for unrelated comments. Skipping them avoids wasted runs and unintended grading.
